knownConsequences.description: AssessmentController.ts:1547 and assessmentInitiativeGenerationRunService.ts:146 are outside this lane's lease and do not catch Postgres error 23505. They must adopt the shared CAS upsert (upsertActiveAssessmentInitiativeBatch) or a concurrent second-batch attempt on those paths will surface as an unhandled 500 instead of reusing the existing active batch.

The Library-to-Workspace click-through with both drdMethodWorkspaceSliceV1 and drdHttpSourceOfTruthV1 flags on is not yet proven end-to-end (no browser/UI evidence). Both flags default false, so no user is affected today.

rollback.mechanism: Revert both commits. The migration's index creation is additive/reversible, but its pre-existing-duplicate reconciliation (marking losing batches 'superseded') is a data mutation that a code revert does not undo — those rows stay superseded, never deleted, so no data is lost either way.
rollback.schemaImpact: one new partial unique index on assessment_initiative_batches; no column changes
rollback.flagImpact: the Library bridge path is gated by drdMethodWorkspaceSliceV1 AND drdHttpSourceOfTruthV1, both default false — reverting the flags alone (no code revert needed) fully restores legacy behaviour for that half
rollback.oldReaderCompatibility: unaffected for the exactly-one-batch fix; the Library bridge path writes zero legacy assessments rows by design (no-dual-write), so old readers of that table see no new rows from the new path

verdictRationale: G0/G1/G3 shared gates pass at this SHA. Both in-lane task suites are fully green on real Postgres (8/8 and 7/7, 15/15 combined) with strong negative controls (concurrency, tenant, replay, cold readback). However this is explicitly NOT a closed guarantee: commit 60a1be98d5 records a KNOWN CONSEQUENCE that two out-of-lease writers (AssessmentController.ts:1547, assessmentInitiativeGenerationRunService.ts:146) do not catch the new unique-index violation and will surface a 500 instead of reusing the active batch until they adopt the shared upsert — this is a blocking integrator change request, not a cosmetic one. Additionally, the Library-to-Workspace click-through (part of this task's user-facing surface) has zero browser/visual evidence and is unproven end-to-end, though it is flag-gated OFF by default so it cannot regress a live user today. Both facts push this below DONE_CURRENT_SHA.
